executive_summary: AGI Infra’s September profit growth reflects faster recognized revenue and margin improvement, but its cash conversion is a more difficult test. FY26 CFO was negative despite positive profit, and a newly reported QIP introduces dilution and deployment questions; this is a regional developer, not a generic consumer company.
research_stance: Growth and margin evidence require cash-collection and project-level validation; avoid valuing recognition-led profit as cash-backed recurring income.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹100.00 crore, +17.6% YoY and +4.2% QoQ. PAT was ₹31.00 crore, +40.9% YoY and +10.7% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹44.00 crore and OPM 44.00%, compared with 39.00% a year earlier and 42.00% in June 2026. PAT margin was 31.00%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

Rounded local sales ₹100 crore and PAT ₹31 crore compare with ₹85 crore/₹22 crore last year. Company-exact numbers reported in public filings are approximately ₹100.19 crore/₹30.74 crore, so rounded local growth differs from exact 17.45%/39.4% calculations. Local operating profit ₹44 crore and OPM 44% are not necessarily comparable to a presentation EBITDA margin using total income; no adjusted EPS or book value from a proposed issue is assumed.

FY26 annual CFO was −₹32 crore and free cash flow −₹52 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹170 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 20.20% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return.

business_economics: Developer accounting and cash arrive on different timelines. Recognized sales can improve with completion mix while land and construction absorb cash. Presales, collections, contract liabilities and remaining construction costs supply the operating bridge. A 44% reported OPM does not prove new projects can earn the same return.

Punjab residential and commercial exposure may benefit from local relationships but concentrates absorption, approvals and land risk. A national property-cycle label cannot support project-level sales or NAV assumptions.
earnings_quality: FY26 CFO was negative ₹32 crore against positive ₹95 crore PAT. This raises a cash-conversion question, not proof of fraud. The test is whether project inventory and remaining construction are matched by recoverable customer collections and adequate funding.

The generic table’s large other-assets field needs to be separated into project inventory, receivables, advances and other assets. Treating it all as bad debt is as incorrect as treating it all as liquid land value. Rounding also changes exact growth percentages without changing the underlying economic direction.
capital_allocation: A placement creates project runway but changes per-share earnings, book value and returns. Do not assume the full reported ₹275 crore authorization has been raised or productively deployed. Actual price, shares, net proceeds and end-use commitments need verification.

The company has an official QIP IR category, but the current document text was not accessible in this review. Launch terms remain attributed reports rather than primary-verified facts. This matters before calculating post-issue NAV or EPS.
valuation_logic: Project NAV should discount expected collections less costs to complete, taxes, finance costs and liabilities. Book value or one-quarter PAT multiplied by four cannot provide that bridge. Land values should not be added on top of an earnings value that already includes the same projects.

The bull case needs good absorption and positive cash conversion with productive proceeds deployment. The base case permits profit growth alongside working-capital absorption. The bear case includes slower collections, repeated external funding and dilution. Dated premium P/E and P/B snapshots do not prove intrinsic value.
peer_positioning: Regional Punjab developers are the closest operating reference where project data exist. DLF, Godrej Properties and Sobha offer NAV or allocation-framework checks, but geography, project mix, approvals and funding differ. A national developer’s multiple does not automatically justify AGI’s premium.
